record.paper_title: Open problems in the Kontsevich graph construction of Poisson bracket symmetries
record.context_brief: Preservation of Nambu-type brackets on R^3
record.original_question: Consider the two-parameter family of Poisson brackets on R^3 defined by {f,g}_{a,ρ}(x,y,z)=ρ(x,y,z)·det(∂(a,f,g)/∂(x,y,z)), where a is a smooth function and ρ is a density in the chosen coordinates. Is this class preserved by any Kontsevich infinitesimal symmetry Ṗ=Q(P), and for a given symmetry does there exist an induced evolutionary system ȧ=A([a],[ρ]), ρ̇=R([a],[ρ]) whose pushforward under τ:(a,ρ)↦{·,·}_{a,ρ} equals Q(P([a],ρ))?

evidence.quote: Problem 11. Is the class of Poisson brackets {·, ·}a,̺ preserved by any of Kontsevich’s infinitesimal symmetries P˙ = Q(P) ? Specifically, for a given symmetry P˙^ij = Q^ij_Pαβ([a], ̺) of the Poisson bi-vector P = (P^ij), does there exist a well defined evolutionary system a˙ = A([a], [̺]), ̺˙ = R([a], [̺]) such that this vector field in the jet space with fibre variables a, ̺ is pushed forward by the tangent map τ∗ to the symmetry Q(P([a], ̺)), here τ : (a, ̺)(x, y, z) ↦ {·, ·}a,̺|(x,y,z) is the linear differential operator.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
On $\mathbb{R}^3$ with coordinates $(x,y,z)$, consider the two-parameter family of Nambu-determinant Poisson brackets
$$\{f,g\}_{a,\rho}(x,y,z) \;=\; \rho(x,y,z)\,\det\!\Big(\tfrac{\partial(a,f,g)}{\partial(x,y,z)}\Big),$$
where $a\in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3)$ is a Casimir function and $\rho\in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3)$ is a density (the bracket is Poisson, i.e. skew-symmetric and Jacobi-satisfying, for every choice of $a,\rho$). Let $P=(P^{ij})$ denote the associated Poisson bi-vector and let
$$\dot P^{ij} \;=\; Q^{ij}_{P\alpha\beta}([a],\rho)$$
be a Kontsevich infinitesimal symmetry of $P$, i.e.\ a bi-vector flow built from a non-trivial cocycle in the Kontsevich graph complex which preserves the Jacobi identity to first order.

Define the linear differential operator
$$\tau:(a,\rho)\longmapsto \{\cdot,\cdot\}_{a,\rho}.$$

(i) Determine whether the class $\{\,\{\cdot,\cdot\}_{a,\rho} : a,\rho\in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3)\,\}$ is preserved under every Kontsevich infinitesimal symmetry $\dot P=Q(P)$.

(ii) For a given Kontsevich symmetry $Q$, decide whether there exists an evolutionary system in the jet space with fibre variables $a,\rho$,
$$\dot a \;=\; A([a],[\rho]),\qquad \dot\rho \;=\; R([a],[\rho]),$$
whose pushforward under the tangent map $\tau_*$ equals $Q(P([a],\rho))$, i.e.
$$\tau_*\!\big(A([a],[\rho]),R([a],[\rho])\big) \;=\; Q\big(P([a],\rho)\big).$$
Describe such $(A,R)$ explicitly when they exist.
artifact.category_tag: Kontsevich graph flows on Nambu–Poisson brackets
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work has established that on $\mathbb{R}^3$ the class of Nambu-determinant Poisson brackets $\{\cdot,\cdot\}_{a,\rho}$ is preserved by the known Kontsevich graph flows (tetrahedral and pentagon-wheel), with explicit evolutionary systems for $(a,\rho)$ realizing the symmetry; the corresponding deformations are trivial in second Poisson cohomology. The general statement for arbitrary Kontsevich symmetries and in higher dimensions remains under active investigation, with dimension-specific obstructions (e.g. invisible graphs) appearing in $d\geq 4$. Thus the problem is partially solved for the originally posed setting on $\mathbb{R}^3$.

status_evidence.title: The hidden symmetry of Kontsevich's graph flows on the spaces of Nambu-determinant Poisson brackets
status_evidence.snippet: Kontsevich's graph flows preserve the class of Nambu-determinant Poisson brackets on R^3 with general density rho; explicit evolutionary systems for (a,rho) are constructed.
status_evidence.claim: Preservation of the Nambu class on R^3 and existence of induced flows on (a,rho) verified for the tetrahedral and pentagon-wheel cocycles.

status_evidence.title: Kontsevich graphs act on Nambu–Poisson brackets, IV
status_evidence.snippet: In dimensions d>=4, invisible graphs that vanish in d=3 become crucial; mechanism differs from the 3D case.
status_evidence.claim: Higher-dimensional generalization remains subtle and is only partially understood.

status_evidence.title: Kontsevich graphs act on Nambu–Poisson brackets, VI. Open problems
status_evidence.snippet: List of remaining open problems on Kontsevich graph action on Nambu-Poisson brackets.
status_evidence.claim: Status as of 2025: progress made, but several aspects remain open.
